claims.text: The initial catalyst is a near-equiatomic multi-principal-element alloy containing Cu, Ni, Pd, and a low level of Pt.
The initial catalyst has a homogeneously distributed surface composition.
ALD at about 150 °C can produce an approximately 2 nm conformal, mesoporous Ce-doped ZrO2 coating on this alloy catalyst.
Calcination at approximately 300 °C will stabilize the porous structure of the deposited coating.
The Ce-doped ZrO2 overlayer will uniformly coat the catalyst without occluding active sites.
Ce3+/Ce4+ redox cycling is associated with oxygen vacancies and enhanced oxygen mobility that can promote CO oxidation.
A Ce-doped ZrO2 overlayer on the proposed multi-principal-element alloy will enhance oxygen mobility.
The enhanced oxygen mobility will lower the activation energy for low-temperature oxidation reactions.
The porous overlayer will limit diffusion of H2O and NO to poisoning-sensitive active sites while retaining reactant access.
The overlayer will physically restrict sintering of the underlying active-metal nanoparticles.
Relative to the unmodified catalyst, the coated catalyst will have a lower CO light-off temperature and achieve efficient CO oxidation below 150 °C.
Relative to the unmodified catalyst, the coated catalyst will achieve improved low-temperature hydrocarbon oxidation below 150 °C.
The coating will reduce activity loss during exposure to H2O and NO.
The coated catalyst will retain better structural integrity and undergo less performance degradation during accelerated aging than the unmodified catalyst.
The combined activity, poison-resistance, and durability benefits will hold under transient automotive exhaust at approximately 100–150 °C containing H2O, NO, and hydrocarbons.
Accelerated aging cycles used in the proposed experiment will simulate extended vehicle mileage.
